label: RITVAYA • DIGESTION
caption:
Most people have heard "drink warm water after food." Fewer know what the classical texts actually say.

In Ayurveda, digestion depends on agni, the digestive fire. The Ashtanga Hridaya describes warm water as light, appetite-kindling and supportive of digestion. It is traditionally used to ease bloating and heaviness.

But the same tradition is specific about amount and timing:
→ Water at the start of a meal can dull appetite.
→ A large amount at the end adds heaviness.
→ Small sips during and after the meal keep things balanced.

What modern research adds:
• Moderate water with meals doesn't harm digestion in healthy people.
• Large volumes stretch the stomach and can worsen reflux in some people.
• Keep it warm, not scalding. Regularly drinking very hot liquids (above about 65 °C) is linked to throat and oesophageal risk.

So the habit isn't "more water." It's the right water, at the right time.

Start with this today: a half cup of warm water, sipped slowly after lunch. Try it for 3 days and observe what changes.

💬 Do you usually drink water before, during or after your meals? Tell us below.

Educational content, not medical advice. If you have a kidney or heart condition, are on fluid restriction, or have ongoing digestive symptoms, follow your doctor's guidance.
